rule: waxaana is the focus particle waxaa plus connective -na 'and'. The form itself does not encode a subject person.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Learner's Somali Grammar (2025), University of Gothenburg
source_example: Waxaana gabi ahaan la xiray waddooyinkaas.
source_analysis: waxaana < waxaa + -na; focus particle + connective and
project_execution: Recognize only exact waxaana when it begins the input sentence, follows an overt clause/sentence boundary, or immediately follows an exact reviewed finite predicate used as a conservative unpunctuated left-clause anchor. Do not infer a hidden subject clitic, antecedent, or verb agreement from the connective particle itself.

rule: waxaana belongs to the waxaa/waxa focus-particle family and is not the person-neutral declarative waana, the statement-clitic wuuna/wayna family, or the baa/ayaa connective-subject-focus family.
source: CONN-WAXAA-001 plus existing project focus/statement distinctions

rule: Exact reviewed waxaa-family connective forms may occur sentence-initial as discourse links as well as clause-initial between main clauses. Executable recognition may use input start or overt punctuation as the left boundary; a narrowly reviewed finite predicate may also license an unpunctuated boundary because -na itself marks the first phrase of the following main clause. The analyzer must not invent or resolve a preceding discourse antecedent.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar, section 14: connective -na is used between main clauses and attaches to the first phrase of the second clause; sentence-initial examples from Learner's Somali Grammar (2025)

rule: waxaana, wuxuuna, waxayna, and waxaadna are independently reviewed exact forms. Their promotion does not license waxana, waxaanan, waxaynuna, waxaadinna, or any other predicted waxa/waxaa+clitic+-na form.
source: Exact-form evidence plus project no-paradigm-generation policy

rule: waxayna is an independently documented connective cleft-focus form for third-person feminine singular or third-person plural subjects, matching the reviewed ay subject-clitic ambiguity.
source: R. David Zorc, Somali-English Dictionary; Morgan Nilsson, Learner's Somali Grammar (2025)
source_examples: Waxayna ogaatay in ay Ugaaso bugto oo ay sariirta jiifto.
project_execution: Allow exact waxayna at input-sentence start, after an overt clause/sentence boundary, or immediately after an exact reviewed finite left-clause predicate; check only encoded 3sg_f/3pl compatibility against exact reviewed finite morphology on the right. Do not infer an antecedent or generate related forms.

rule: waxaadna is independently attested as connective 'and you ...'; its base waxaad is documented as focus plus second-person subject pronoun/clitic, matching the reviewed aad 2sg/2pl ambiguity.
source: R. David Zorc, English-Somali Finder List for waxaad; exact waxaadna attested repeatedly in Mahmud Muhammad Abduh's Somali Qur'an translation
source_examples: Waxaadna ku cabbaysaan Biyo kulayl badan.
project_execution: Allow exact waxaadna at input-sentence start, after an overt clause/sentence boundary, or immediately after an exact reviewed finite left-clause predicate; check only encoded 2sg/2pl compatibility against exact reviewed finite morphology on the right. Do not infer an antecedent or generate related forms.

rule: For exact wuxuuna/waxayna/waxaadna, agreement may be judged only when an exact reviewed finite verb is found in the local predicate window. Unknown predicates remain unjudged. waxaana remains person-neutral and never inherits this agreement rule.

Sentence-initial surface position is independently attested for each listed exact reviewed form; therefore punctuation from a preceding clause is not required inside the input string. The connective meaning may refer to prior discourse that is outside the analyzed string.

rule: The connective suffix -na is a main-clause conjunction attached to the first phrase of the second clause; punctuation is not part of its morphological composition. For unpunctuated executable recognition, the project requires the exact connective surface to immediately follow an exact reviewed finite verb, which acts only as a conservative left-clause anchor.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar, section 14 coordination: -na is used between main clauses and attaches to the first phrase of the second clause
project_execution: Do not treat any arbitrary mid-sentence waxaana/wuxuuna/waxayna/waxaadna as licensed. Require lexical adjacency to an exact reviewed finite left predicate and no intervening clause punctuation. If the left predicate is unknown or non-finite, leave the unpunctuated construction unjudged. This heuristic does not assert that Somali grammar universally requires a clause-final verb or forbids omitted punctuation.

rule: wuxuuna is the independently documented masculine singular waxaa-family connective focus form, carrying subject clitic uu plus connective -na.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Aasaaska Ortogaraafiga Afka Soomaaliga, section on Waxa(a) + xiriiriyaha -na; Morgan Nilsson, Kontrastiv Somalisk Grammatik, -na coordination examples
source_examples: Wax yar ka dib waxa u yimi nin socoto ah, wuxuuna weydiiyey sababta ka oohisay.
project_execution: Recognize exact wuxuuna with reviewed 3sg_m subject compatibility. Do not derive other waxaa-family connectives by analogy.

rule: The waxa/waxaa focus construction places the focused noun phrase or other focused complement after the verb: waxa(a) + subject clitic + VERB + focused material. Therefore a clitic-bearing waxaa-family connective followed by an exact reviewed finite verb but no lexical material after that verb is structurally unsupported by the reviewed final-focus pattern and should be reviewed rather than accepted as a neutral statement.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar: waxa(a)/waxaa expresses that the noun phrase at the end of the clause is focused; documented word order waxa(a) + subject pronoun + verb + final focused noun phrase
project_execution: For exact wuxuuna/waxayna/waxaadna, if an exact reviewed finite verb is found, record whether lexical material follows it in the same analyzed clause. If none follows, mark the focus structure for REVIEW, not autofix. Do not automatically replace the form with wuuna/wayna/other statement forms because ellipsis or broader discourse may exist and not every statement-person connective is independently reviewed.

rule: A clitic-bearing second clause may grammatically change subject, so an incompatible subject clitic is not automatically an error. However, when the immediately preceding clause contains a reviewed statement subject clitic and the second clause begins with a waxaa-family connective whose encoded person set is disjoint, the sentence should be marked context-required rather than plain-correct if no separate antecedent is established inside the analyzed text.
source: Reviewed subject-clitic person mappings plus the source-backed fact that -na joins distinct main clauses; project distinction between grammatical agreement and discourse antecedent resolution
project_execution: Compare only exact reviewed left statement clitics wuu/way/waad with exact right connective subject clitics uu/ay/aad. Overlap means same-subject continuation is compatible. Disjoint sets mean subject continuity is context-required, not a grammatical-error autofix. Do not infer that the second subject must equal the first subject.
